## Maple Syrup Yield and Sugaring Season Temperature

### Data Preparation

Load libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

Weather data

```{r}
#read weather data txt file
weather <- read_table(
  "climdiv-tmpcst-v1.0.0-20261006.txt",
  col_names = FALSE
) %>%
  select(-X14) %>% #remove extra blank column
  rename( #rename columns with month abbreviations
    id = X1,
    jan = X2,
    feb = X3,
    mar = X4,
    apr = X5,
    may = X6,
    jun = X7,
    jul = X8,
    aug = X9,
    sep = X10,
    oct = X11,
    nov = X12,
    dec = X13
  ) %>%
  mutate( #extract information from id based on NOAA documentation
    state_code = substr(id, 1, 3),
    division = substr(id, 4, 4),
    element = substr(id, 5, 6),
    year = as.integer(substr(id, 7, 10))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      jan:dec,
      ~ na_if(.x, -99.9) #replace missing values (-99.9) with NA
    )
  )
```

Subset data by state and year

```{r}
maple_states_weather <- weather %>%
  filter( #Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, Vermont, and Wisconsin
    state_code %in% c("017", "020", "027", "030", 
                      "036", "043", "047"),
    division == "0", #0 indicates an area-averaged element
    element == "02", # 02 = Average Temperature
    year >= 2001,
    year <= 2026
  )
```

Average sugaring season temperature and add state column

```{r}
maple_states_weather <- maple_states_weather %>%
  mutate(
    avg_temp = rowMeans(
      select(., feb, mar, apr), #average temperature with sugaring months
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
  state = recode(
    state_code, #create new state column
    "017" = "Maine",
    "020" = "Michigan",
    "027" = "New Hampshire",
    "030" = "New York",
    "036" = "Pennsylvania",
    "043" = "Vermont",
    "047" = "Wisconsin"
  )
)
```

Select relevant columns in new dataframe

```{r}
maple_avg_temp <- maple_states_weather %>%
  select(state, year, avg_temp)
```

Yield data

```{r}
#read yield data csv file
yield <- read_csv("2C6116DA-646B-3D00-8F9F-03225D4D016B.csv") %>%
  select(State, Year, Value) %>% #select relevant columns
  rename( #rename columns
    state = State,
    year = Year,
    gal_tap = Value
  ) %>%
  mutate( #change capitalization to match weather data states
    state = str_to_title(state)
  )
```

Combine datasets

```{r}
maple_analysis <- yield %>%
  left_join(maple_avg_temp, by = c("state", "year")) %>%
  select(state, year, avg_temp, gal_tap)

head(maple_analysis)
```

### Research question

**Is average temperature during the maple sugaring season (February–April) associated with syrup yield per tap across seven U.S. states from 2001–2026?**

**Null hypothesis (H₀):** There is no association between February–April average temperature and maple syrup yield per tap, after accounting for year and state.

**Alternative hypothesis (H₁):** There is an association between February–April average temperature and maple syrup yield per tap, after accounting for year and state.

### Cases

Each case represents one state in one year. The dataset includes seven maple-producing states (Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, Vermont, and Wisconsin) across 26 years (2001–2026), for a total of **182 observations.**

### Data collection

This project will use two publicly available datasets:

1.  [**USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS):**](https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/) Annual maple syrup yield, measured in gallons per tap, for the seven selected states from 2001–2026.

2.  [**NOAA nClimDiv:**](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/metadata/landing-page/bin/iso?id=gov.noaa.ncdc:C00005) Monthly statewide average temperature data. Observations for February, March, and April will be used to calculate the average temperature during the sugaring season for each state and year.

The datasets will be combined by state and year so that each observation includes the corresponding yield and average temperature.

### Study type

This is an **observational** study because the project uses historical yield and weather data. The analysis will examine associations rather than establish causation.

### Data sources

[USDA NASS Quick Stats](https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/) Retrieved 11/04/2026

[NOAA nClimDiv Monthly Data](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/data/nclimdiv-monthly/access/) Retrieved 11/04/2026

### Variables

**Response variable:**

- Maple syrup yield per tap: Numerical variable, measured in gallons per tap.

**Explanatory variables:**

- Average sugaring-season temperature: Numerical variable, calculated as the average of February, March, and April temperatures for each state and year. This is the primary explanatory variable.

- Year: Numerical variable ranging from 2001–2026.

**Categorical variable:**

- State: Categorical variable identifying the seven states

### Summary statistics

Overall

```{r}
summary_overall <- maple_analysis %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(avg_temp, gal_tap),
      list(
        mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  )

summary_overall
```

By state

```{r}
summary_by_state <- maple_analysis %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      c(avg_temp, gal_tap),
      list(
        mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        min = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        max = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_by_state
```

Average temperature vs. maple syrup yield

```{r}
ggplot(maple_analysis, aes(x = avg_temp, y = gal_tap)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature vs. Maple Syrup Yield",
    x = "Average Temperature (°F)",
    y = "Gallons per Tap"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Maple syrup yield over time by state

```{r}
ggplot(maple_analysis, aes(x = year, y = gal_tap, color = state)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Maple Syrup Yield Over Time",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Gallons per Tap",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
